c6_board.title: The board, last time
c6_board.text: The board in the square is crowded now with notices in a dozen hands. Near the bottom is the old one, the lost glove. It is still there. Nobody ever claimed it. You find this very funny.

pages.text: The second orchard goes in, row on row, a green stair up the hill. Down in the first orchard, the old swing is still moving, just a little, as if somebody has only just got off.
On the plank lies an apple core, eaten down to the pips. You do not need to know who. The knot holds.

c6_seed_library.title: A shelf of small tomorrows
c6_seed_library.text: Rows of tiny envelopes, each with a name in a different hand. Carrot. Bean. “Maud's good pumpkin.” “Do not lose.” They rustle faintly when you walk past. A shelf full of next summer, put in order. You find yourself walking quietly, the way you would in front of sleeping people.

c6_oven.title: The big oven
c6_oven.text: The big oven takes six loaves at once and rises to the occasion. The whole lane smells of it. A queue forms that nobody organised. Hilde is in it, pretending to be in the way. Old Jan is behind her, very much not pretending.

c6_whirligig.title: The singing pole
c6_whirligig.text: The wind pump spins. The pole sings a small, silly song, and the water comes up out of the ground as though it had been waiting for its turn. You stand there with your hands on your hips, listening. From the coop, the hens give an opinion about the noise. It is not kind.

c6_dye.title: The blue vat
c6_dye.text: You lift the cloth out of the vat, and it is green, an ugly, wet, mud-sort-of green. Then the air touches it, and it turns blue. Slowly. Like a thought arriving. You hold it, dripping, and watch it become the colour of a sky that has been waiting its turn.

c6_theatre.title: The cheese play
c6_theatre.text: The travelling theatre's play is about a cheese. It is a great cheese. It gets lost, and found, and mistaken for the moon. The lead actor holds your cheese wheel very still for the whole second act. You have never seen anyone so serious about a cheese.

c6_agnes.title: Thyme
c6_agnes.text: Elder Agnes sprinkles the thyme over your tapenade as though dealing cards. “Your grandmother put this in everything,” she says. “She had a saying. 'If in doubt, thyme.'” You wait for the rest. There is no rest. That was the whole saying. Somehow it is enough to keep.

c6_flags.title: Bunting
c6_flags.text: The flags go up between the houses, a hundred small triangles, red and yellow and blue and one that is nobody's colour. The wind finds them and they all lean the same way at once. It makes the whole square look as if it were about to say something good.

c6_orphanage.title: Jam and a spoon
c6_orphanage.text: At the long table by the orphanage window, the jam goes round on thick slices of your bread. Nobody speaks, because everyone's mouth is full. One small child puts the empty jar to her ear, as though a little of the summer might still be in there. Matron Elsie pretends not to see.

c6_well.title: The village well
c6_well.text: The well stands finished, a ring of grey stone, and the first bucket comes up on its rope. The water is so clear you can see your own face in it. Behind your face, a row of other faces, leaning in. All of Hazelwood is trying to look into the same hole at once.

c6_telescope.title: Stars
c6_telescope.text: The astronomer at the telescope waves you over. “Look,” Vega says, and steps back. At first, black. Then a smear of silver, and then it is not a smear. It is hundreds. You say nothing. After a long time Vega says, quietly, “Yes. That is what I say, too.”

pages.text: Kit wraps the rainbow scarf three times round and declares it “every colour of every thought I almost had.”
Then Kit writes it down. Then Kit reads it aloud, to you, to the cow, and to a passing man who was only asking the way. He says it is very good, and that the way is left.

c6_painter.title: Saffron
c6_painter.text: The painter mixes the saffron into a little pot, and the pot goes gold. She paints one stroke across the paper, and a field is suddenly there, in the afternoon, with the light on it. “Thank you,” she says. She looks as if she means for the whole season.

c6_quilt.title: A patchwork
c6_quilt.text: Spread across the linen on your bed, a patchwork cover, every square a different cloth. You can pick out a few: Maud's checked apron, a scrap of blue, something that smells faintly of lavender. All of Hazelwood, sewn together by people you have not quite caught doing it.

pages.text: Evening. You light the fire in the yard, the first thing you ever lit here. The spark takes on the first try. The ash around it glows a little, as if it remembers something.
You sit with your back against the fence you built. The bucket, by the door, is full of rain. None of this was here when you came. Now you are sitting in the middle of it.

c6_n_seed.title: In the margin
c6_n_seed.text: “Always save the best one for next year. And the second best, for a neighbour.”

c6_n_worms.title: In the margin
c6_n_worms.text: Next to the worms: “They do the real work. Call them by name.” A list follows. They are all called Gerald.

c6_n_soil.title: In the margin
c6_n_soil.text: “A handful of living soil has more creatures in it than there are people. Remember that when you feel small.”

c6_n_last.title: In the margin
c6_n_last.text: You turn to the last page in the book. It is empty. Only, in the margin, in a hand you know so well by now: “Well. Look at that. You read all of it. Go and put the kettle on, my love.”

c6_k_summer.text: The long evening light lies across the fields like a cat that owns them.

c6_k_fair.text: Somewhere in the square a drum is being tested, and then, firmly, forbidden.

c6_k_alpaca.text: The alpaca looks at you with enormous patience. She has seen more than she lets on. She is not telling.

c6_k_garden.text: Dusk. White flowers open, one by one, as though somebody were turning the lights up on a small, private party.
